Whole pies, baked thin and crispy. No slices of pizza, the pie is the point.

The first restaurant

Anthony Falco finally has a room of his own.

Pizzeria the Pantheon Bar is the first restaurant of Anthony Falco, the pizzaiolo who helped turn Roberta's in Bushwick into a destination. This time the room is his, opened outright with his partner Mateo Vivas.

The idea is simple and strict. Pies come whole, thin and crispy. Around them, a short menu that knows what it is: focaccia by the slice, radicchio, beans. Nothing extra, nothing apologetic.

One pie, built in front of you.

Keep going. The slices find each other.

Slice one finds its place.At the Pantheon, the pie is served whole. This is how it comes together.

Short menu, no shortcuts.

Four things, done properly. That was the menu the room opened with, and it is the whole argument: a pie, a slice of focaccia, something bitter, something simple.

Whole Pies

Thin and crispy, baked whole and brought to the table as one pie. Order it for the table, or keep it all to yourself.

The main event

Focaccia by the Slice

A thick, golden slice with a soft, open middle. The quick order, the first order, the one you eat while you decide on a pie.

By the slice

Radicchio

The bitter leaf, served as a salad. Sharp and refreshing next to a hot, crisp pie.

Something bitter

Beans

A simple bowl of beans alongside the pies. Plain, warm and exactly enough.

Something simple

Pantheon Passport: the guest chef series.

The room opened with a passport in hand. Pantheon Passport brings guest chefs to Grand Street to cook their own take on the pie.

The series launched with Defne and Emre Kasrat of Gusina, Istanbul, serving Turkish inspired pizzas, including a smoked ribeye pizza, the Füme Antrikot.

Series launched Wednesday 25 November 2026.
